title: Relative normalization and Zariski main theorem for representable stack maps
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $f:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose their diagonals are quasi-compact and separated, in the scheme-chart conventions of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Suppose $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], quasi-finite and separated: its scheme base changes are algebraic-space morphisms of finite type with finite geometric fibres and closed relative diagonal [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Form the quasi-coherent algebra $f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ on the smooth-etale site of $\mathcal V$ [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Its integral-closure subalgebra $\mathcal A$ is characterized as follows: on every smooth affine scheme chart $T\to\mathcal V$, its sections are the elements of $\Gamma(\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T,\mathcal O)$ satisfying a monic polynomial with coefficients in $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. This prescription defines a quasi-coherent subalgebra and commutes with smooth base change. The relative spectrum $\mathcal N=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{\mathcal V}\mathcal A$ is the stack whose scheme base change to $T$ is the scheme obtained by gluing the spectra of this algebra on affine opens of $T$. It is an algebraic stack with quasi-compact separated diagonal. The projection $h:\mathcal N\to\mathcal V$ is integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and the evaluation map $j:\mathcal U\to\mathcal N$ is a quasi-compact open immersion with $hj\simeq f$. Here open immersion means that every scheme base change is an open subscheme. Moreover $h_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal N}=\mathcal A\subseteq f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$, with inclusion induced by $j$.

source.place: Tag 082J (lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine), Tag 082F (lemma-normalization-smooth-localization); spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0820 (lemma-integral-closure) and Tag 0ABP (lemma-properties-normalization). Smooth descent gives the representable algebraic-stack form used in Alper Lemma 8.3.1, citing LMB Theorem 16.5. The explicit integral-closure version is the smooth-local extension of these Stacks statements.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to\mathcal V$, put $U_T=\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T$. The hypothesis gives a separated finite-type algebraic space $U_T\to T$ whose geometric fibres $U_T\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ have finitely many points. By the finite-fibre criterion for separated finite-type spaces, applied at every $t\in T$ with $K$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$, the map is quasi-finite at every point of $|U_T|$; that is, every representable etale scheme chart $V\to U_T$ has $V\to T$ locally quasi-finite. With the closed-immersion diagonal, the schemehood lemma makes $U_T$ a scheme. Its morphism to $T$ is separated and finite type, hence quasi-compact. The scheme-test criterion makes $f$ quasi-compact as a stack map. Its relative diagonal is a closed immersion on scheme tests, hence affine and quasi-compact; its own diagonal is an isomorphism, so it is also quasi-separated. Thus $f$ satisfies the quasi-compact quasi-separated hypotheses of the algebra direct-image theorem. Apply that theorem to obtain $\mathcal B=f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$, whose restriction on every smooth scheme test $T$ is $\Gamma(U_T,\mathcal O)$. This is the $f_*\mathcal O$ of the statement, on its specified smooth-etale site.

source.place: Tag 03XX; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 050T; stacks-cohomology.tex Tags 077A and 0GQQ; decent-spaces.tex Tag 0ACK (lemma-conditions-on-fibre-and-qf) for the finite-fibre criterion.

proof.text: Choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $P\to\mathcal V$ and replace $P$ by the disjoint union of its affine opens. Write $R=P\times_{\mathcal V}P$; its projections are smooth. On $P$ take the integral-closure subalgebra $C=\operatorname{IC}_P(\mathcal B|_P)$ supplied by the existing closure lemma. The smooth-pullback comparison identifies each $p_i^*C$ with the integral closure in $\mathcal B|_R$. Consequently the canonical descent isomorphism of $\mathcal B$ restricts to an isomorphism $p_1^*C\simeq p_2^*C$. Its identity and cocycle equations hold because both sides are restrictions of the same equations in $\mathcal B$, and the inclusions on these smooth relation spaces are injective. Smooth-atlas algebra descent now produces a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A$ and a map $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, injective on the smooth-etale site. This constructs a subalgebra on exactly the site in the statement; no nonflat pullback of a monomorphism is asserted.

source.place: Tag 06WV(1),(5), using spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 0820 and spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 082E.

proof.text: For any smooth scheme test $T\to\mathcal V$, the projections from $P\times_{\mathcal V}T$ to $P$ and to $T$ are smooth, and the latter is surjective. Apply smooth pullback of integral closure on this relation space. It identifies the pullback of $\mathcal A|_T$ with the pullback of $\operatorname{IC}_T(\mathcal B|_T)$, compatibly with inclusions into $\mathcal B$. Take a surjective etale scheme chart of this relation space; its composite to $T$ is a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Full faithfulness of smooth descent on this atlas identifies the two algebras on $T$. If $T$ is affine, the closure lemma and the smooth-test direct-image formula give precisely the stated monic-polynomial description. The same comparison for a further smooth morphism of stacks can be checked on smooth scheme atlases of its source, so the prescription commutes with smooth base change. The canonical identifications satisfy composition because their maps into the ambient algebra agree. They also prove independence of the chosen atlas and uniqueness of $\mathcal A$.

source.place: Tag 082E and Tag 082F, smooth-local algebra comparison; stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06WV.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal N=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{\mathcal V}\mathcal A$ using the existing stack relative-spectrum construction. It is algebraic, $h$ is representable by schemes and affine, and for every scheme $t:T\to\mathcal V$ its pullback is $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_T(t^*\mathcal A)$ with the required affine-open gluing and arbitrary-base-change compatibility. The same theorem identifies $h_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_{\mathcal N}$ with $\mathcal A$. Under the algebra adjunction for $f$, the inclusion $\mathcal A\to f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$ gives an algebra map $f^*\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal U}$. On objects this sends $u\in\mathcal U(T)$ to $(f(u),u^*f^*\mathcal A\to\mathcal O_T)$ in the defining pair description of $\mathcal N(T)$; naturality gives its arrows. It is the evaluation morphism $j$, with $hj\simeq f$. Its induced structure-sheaf map is the original inclusion by adjunction.

source.place: Tag 01LX; algebraic.tex Tag 05UM; the stack extension is by the pair functor and algebra adjunction.

proof.text: Let $T\to\mathcal V$ be smooth affine. Step 1 supplies a separated finite-type quasi-finite scheme map $U_T\to T$; $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its relative normalization has affine ring over $T$ equal to the integral closure of $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ in $\Gamma(U_T,\mathcal O)$. Moreover the canonical map from $U_T$ pulls back functions by the inclusion of this ring. Steps 3 and 4 therefore identify this normalization, including its canonical map, with $\mathcal N_T$ and $j_T$. The scheme Zariski main theorem makes $h_T$ integral and $j_T$ a quasi-compact open immersion. All its hypotheses are verified here on an affine base; no global quasi-compactness of $\mathcal V$ is used.

source.place: Tag 02LR; morphisms.tex Tags 035F, 035H and 035I, including the affine-ring identification.

proof.text: For an arbitrary affine scheme $T\to\mathcal V$, pull back the smooth atlas $P\to\mathcal V$. Smooth local sections supply an etale cover of $T$ lifting to $P$. Refine it by affine opens mapping to individual affine components of $P$, and take a finite subfamily covering the quasi-compact $T$. This is an fpqc cover by affine schemes $T_i$. Each $h_{T_i}$ is a base change of the integral scheme map over that affine component of $P$ from step 5. The ring base-change theorem preserves integrality, so fpqc descent of integral scheme morphisms makes $h_T$ integral. Integrality for nonaffine $T$ is the same affine-open condition in the definition of an integral morphism. Thus $h$ is integral on every scheme test. Notice that $t^*\mathcal A$ on a nonsmooth test is tensor pullback; we have not replaced it by an integral closure computed after a possibly nonflat base change.

source.place: Tag 02L9; more-morphisms.tex Tag 0CFV; tensor pullback in Tag 01LX.

proof.text: The scheme $\mathcal N_P$ is a smooth surjective atlas of $\mathcal N$, since it is the base change of $P\to\mathcal V$. Step 5 identifies $\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal N}\mathcal N_P=\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}P$ with an open subscheme of $\mathcal N_P$. Its two pullbacks to the relation space agree: both are pullbacks of the global morphism $j$ and its image. Invariant-open descent therefore gives an open substack $W\subseteq\mathcal N$ through which $j$ factors. This factor $\mathcal U\to W$ becomes an isomorphism after the smooth atlas just used. To see it is an equivalence, pull objects and arrows to that cover: arrows descend uniquely by the sheaf condition on Isom, and the locally unique lifts of objects have a unique compatible descent datum, effective by fppf stack descent. Hence $\mathcal U\simeq W$, and $j$ is an open immersion on every scheme test. The fppf-descent theorem applies to both algebraic stacks; it does not assume a Deligne--Mumford atlas.

source.place: Tag 0507 (open case); criteria.tex Tag 076V for effective fppf descent.

proof.text: For any scheme $T\to\mathcal V$, the factorization $U_T\xrightarrow{j_T}\mathcal N_T\xrightarrow{h_T}T$ has quasi-compact composite, since $f_T$ is finite type. Its second map is affine, hence separated and quasi-separated. Quasi-compact cancellation for algebraic spaces gives that $j_T$ is quasi-compact. For a scheme $Q\to\mathcal N$, put $T=Q$ with its composite map to $\mathcal V$. The map $\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal N}Q\to Q$ is the pullback of $j_T$ along the section $Q\to\mathcal N_T$ determined by $Q\to\mathcal N$. Base-change stability gives its quasi-compactness. The representable scheme-test criterion proves that $j$ is quasi-compact as a stack morphism.

Finally factor the absolute diagonal as $\mathcal N\xrightarrow{\Delta_h}\mathcal N\times_{\mathcal V}\mathcal N\to\mathcal N\times_k\mathcal N$. The second arrow is the pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal V}$ by the diagonal fibre-product identity. The first is a closed immersion on scheme tests: $h$ is affine, so its scheme-test diagonals are closed immersions. Thus the first is affine and quasi-compact, and the second is quasi-compact by hypothesis and base-change stability. The stack quasi-compact quasi-separated composition theorem gives quasi-compactness of their composite (each factor is quasi-separated, the first being affine and the second being a base change of a separated representable map). Separation of both representable factors and separation permanence give separation of this composite. Consequently $\mathcal N$ has quasi-compact separated diagonal. Together with steps 4, 6, 7 and 8 this proves every asserted property, with the specified inclusion on the smooth-etale site.
